item.title: Seahawks get bad news as new OL Quenton Nelson ruled out for Week 9
item.description: Seahawks get bad news as new OL Quenton Nelson ruled out for Week 9 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks lost to the Chicago Bears in Week 8 in a Monday Night matchup that featured a fun storyline of two recent trade pickups, with Quenton Nelson at left guard for the Seahawks and Jeffery Simmons at defensive tackle for the Bears. While the Seahawks lost the battle there, and the game as a whole, there are still plenty of things to be confident about with this team. But, unfortunately, heading into Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals , the Seahawks got some bad news. According to Gregg Bell of 93.3 KJR radio , the Seahawks will not have Nelson in Week 9, as he's been ruled out by head coach Mike Macdonald due to a knee issue that will have him week to week going forward. Quenton Nelson ruled out for Week 9 amid knee injury "OUT: ... Quenton Nelson 'minor procedure, not IR'... Nelson 'had something he was dealing with when he got here,' from Colts trade, Mike Macdonald," Bell reports. Macdonald told reporters on Friday that Nelson, the Seahawks' recent Pro Bowl offensive guard addition, will miss Week 9, and also potentially Week 10 as he deals with a knee issue. He's having a minor procedure on his knee and will miss the Cardinals matchup. With the team's Week 11 bye, it stands to reason that the Seahawks will hold Nelson, their big trade pickup, out for Week 10 as well. MORE : Why it's time for Colts to move on from Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones The next time the Seahawks get Nelson might be in Week 12, when they face off against the San Francisco 49ers in what could be a pivotal matchup for the NFC West division title. What's important to note about this injury is that it's not a new problem, and it's something the Seahawks reportedly knew before they acquired him from the Colts. While Nelson will miss a week, maybe more, he should be able to come back this season when it matters most. Just for the next week or so, Anthony Bradford will take back over. The Seahawks are fortunate they face the Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders these next two weeks, which are matchups they should be able to win, even if Nelson is out. item.title: International snub could be a blessing in disguise for Manchester City left-back
item.description: International snub could be a blessing in disguise for Manchester City left-back Nico O’Reilly hasn’t been at his best do far this season for Manchester City. A back injury he suffered in the warm-up before Manchester City’s 1-0 win over Coventry City back at the beginning of September has hampered the England international. Also, O’Reilly had a busy 2025-26 season where he played 53 matches in all competitions for City and earned himself a spot in the England squad for the 2026 World Cup. Nico O’Reilly entered the 2026-27 season having played his first full season and had a busy summer. So far this season he hasn’t been at his best. This has culminated in O’Reilly missing out on selection in England’s squad for the upcoming internationals, which could be a blessing in disguise for him and Manchester City. Enzo Maresca believes that the opportunity to rest and recuperate is ideal for Nico O’Reilly. Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca was asked about Nico O’Reilly being left out of the England squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain when he faced the media on Friday. Maresca believes that O’Reilly now has an opportunity to rest and recuperate and come back after the international break at 100%. He explained when asked about O’Reilly being left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad: “ With Nico it’s quite easy. Since we started the season, between his back, if you remember before the Coventry game he’s had more problems unfortunately. ” “ He’s not 100% but in the last game I really liked him and thought he played a very good game. ” “ This is what we need from Nico. We just need to keep him fit because we know how good he is and I have no doubt in future he’ll be in the international team again. ” “ It’s what he needs – to use the break to do the right things in terms of therapy and these kind of things to be 100% after the break. ” Manchester City will be hoping that some time away from football will pay off for Nico O’Reilly. Nico O’Reilly has not been at his best so far this season. Niggling injuries and a hectic schedule looks to have caught up to him. With how important Nico O’Reilly is to Enzo Maresca’s side and with how much football is played by City the opportunity to rest for players like Nico O’Reilly is few and far between. Also, it must be remembered that O’Reilly is only 21 and has only played one full season of first-team football followed by playing in a World Cup. Eventually everything was going to catch up to O’Reilly. That is what has transpired. Not being selected in the England squad by Thomas Tuchel for their upcoming matches against Croatia and Spain does give Nico O’Reilly the opportunity to rest. He needs it. It is a rare opportunity for him and hopefully he and Manchester City see the benefits of this after the upcoming international break. item.title: Emerling Skipping Homestead O’Reilly Race to Be With Growing Family
item.description: Patrick Emerling has had a pretty incredible 2026 season as far as his racing endeavors are concerned. The driver won the championship for the first time in the NASCAR Whelen Modified Tour, and he has made five starts combined in the NASCAR National Series. This weekend, Emerling was set to add another NASCAR National Series start to his resume, as he was slated to compete behind the wheel of the No. 38 RSS Racing entry in Saturday’s NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway, but on Friday, Emerling revealed on social media that he will not travel to Homestead this weekend. Just wanted to provide an update about this weekends O’Reilly event at Homestead. ? My family & I are expecting a new addition, likely this weekend. With that, I have decided to step out of the car & stay home with them. I love racing, but family comes first! pic.twitter.com/2VprYNG1J7 — Patrick Emerling (@PatrickEmerling) November 6, 2026 “Just wanted to provide an update about this weekend’s O’Reilly event at Homestead,” Emerling said in his post on X . “My family and I are expecting a new addition, likely this weekend. With that, I have decided to step out of the car & stay home with them. I love racing, but family comes first!” Even though he won’t be behind the wheel this weekend, Emerling will still be a winner, as he is set to become a three-time dad. In 64 career starts in the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, Emerling has a career-best finish of 10th, which he achieved in the 2025 season-opening event at Daytona International Speedway. RSS Racing has yet to announce who, if anyone, will step in for Emerling behind the wheel of the No. 38 Ford this weekend. item.title: Tosh Lupoi's seat heating up as Cal prepares for crucial stretch of football
item.description: Cal head coach Tosh Lupoi is seen during the first quarter against Wagner on Sept. 19 in Berkeley. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) If the firewood under Tosh Lupoi's seat hadn't caught a spark already, it's certainly begun to smoke. As Cal football prepares to navigate the last three games of what's been a disappointing season (3-6, 2-4 ACC) - a stretch that could very well determine the direction of the program, as well as the first-year head coach's tenure in Berkeley - general manager Ron Rivera lit a matchstick on the KNBR airwaves, setting the stakes for the final month. "The biggest thing I can tell you guys is - again, I know expectations were very, very high, and I know there's the comparison to UCLA, but the thing everybody's gotta understand is UCLA brought in a current head coach that came and brought probably half of the team that he had that went to the playoff to begin with," Rivera said on Thursday on the "Murph & Markus Show" amidst the Bears' bye week. "Tosh came in as a first-time head coach. He did bring a couple of inexperienced coordinators with him. Things didn't work out the way we needed them to work out on offense." "He has bumped his head a lot. We have talked a lot, tried to give him a lot of advice, point him in the right direction. Some of it, he's been very receptive, and other portions of it, he hasn't. And it's those things that sometimes you've gotta learn for yourself before you think, ‘Oh wow, this is it.' But I'd like to continue to stress that this is a guy that's learning, growing. But now it's time. These last three games, hopefully four, the trajectory has to be going north. We have to show that we are growing; there has been some growth and development of our players, our team, and the culture is getting stronger. Those are all things that you have to have going forward." In just 60 seconds on the radio, Rivera laid out the terms of Cal's season in a nutshell. The Bears had hype that they didn't live up to. The Bears have taken their lumps through growing pains, but have little to show for it. And the Bears will have their opportunities to demonstrate they've become a stronger team, with a winnable 3-game slate against Virginia, Stanford and Pitt that can grant them bowl eligibility if they run the table. But as Rivera intimated, a chunk of the fiasco Cal finds itself in – a loss away from no bowl game, with a flimsy case to present to star quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele as to why he should return next year – lands on how Lupoi has guided the Bears. To recap: Cal ranks 132nd in the country in expected points added per play (-0.23), 132nd in offensive EPA/play (-0.13), and 93rd in defensive EPA/play according to Game on Paper , with only the latter being marginally better than the 2025 Bears. In its six losses, Cal has been outscored 239-102 and a combined 120-41 in the second halves of those games. The Bears rank second to last in penalties per game (9.1) and dead last in penalty yards per game (84.8).

item.title: Jesús de Miguel death sparks urgent plea for soccer medical rule change
item.description: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel tragically died on Tuesday -Credit:Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images Following the tragic death of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel , physiotherapist Antonio Pérez has called for a rule change in soccer that would allow medical personnel to enter the field without requiring the referee's authorization. According to a preliminary autopsy report, De Miguel died from 'accidental chest trauma' after sustaining a severe collision during a match against FC Andorra. The incident unfolded in the 97th minute as De Miguel sprinted toward the ball. Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono charged out of his area, attempting to clear it, but collided forcefully with the striker, striking him hard in the chest. Owono received a red card, while De Miguel was treated on the field before suffering a cardiac arrest. The striker was rushed by ambulance to Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria, where doctors initially succeeded in stabilizing his condition. Tragically, however, he passed away on Tuesday morning. The match was abandoned following the incident, with the Royal Spanish Football Federation suspending all fixtures until Friday. Pérez subsequently took to social media to extend his condolences to De Miguel's family while highlighting what he considers to be a critical change needed in soccer to better safeguard players. In a video, the physiotherapist urged governing authorities to reassess the regulations dictating how rapidly medical staff can respond to on-field emergencies. He said via The Mirror : "There is a rule in football that needs to change: as a professional, as a medical practitioner, I should be able to step in at the slightest sign of concern. "'Get up already!' - a phrase I heard so often while working on the pitch. Yesterday, Jesús de Miguel did not get up. And I want you to look closely at the play. More than 10 seconds pass from the moment of the unfortunate collision until medical staff arrive. "This is because the referee chooses to issue a red card before attending to the player. The more time that passes, the lower the likelihood of recovery. This applies not only to cardiac events but also to more common types of concussions, such as head concussions. item.title: Ferrari's Hamilton-Leclerc problem - and other F1 stories to follow
item.description: Charles Leclerc trails Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton by 14 points in the drivers' championship [Getty Images] The drivers' title is sewn up, and the constructors' may well be on Sunday, but Formula 1 marches restlessly, relentlessly on. This weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix is in many ways the first page of the first chapter of the next championship battle. New world champion Kimi Antonelli says he sees the final races of the season as preparation to defend his title in 2027, and his vanquished Mercedes team-mate George Russell is working on understanding where things went wrong, with the aim of putting them right. The team's main target this weekend is securing the three points more than Ferrari they need to lock away the constructors' championship, to underline their return to the form they showed for so long in the 2010s. Mercedes' rivals, meanwhile, are continuing the work that has seen them turn what was a chasm in performance at the beginning of the year into a highly competitive battle between the top four teams at the end. The season has been in two parts. Mercedes dominated the first third, winning seven of the first eight races. Since then, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have all had their time in the sun, and out of the past 12 races, Mercedes have won six, Red Bull three, McLaren two and Ferrari one. Only the beginnings of a competitive picture have emerged in Sao Paulo, with Antonelli and Lando Norris in an upgraded McLaren initially appearing in good shape in Friday practice, but beyond that there are a number of running narratives to maintain the interest. The Hamilton-Leclerc problem Ferrari boss has to solve Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc damaged their own chances on the first lap in Mexico last weekend, which opened the door for Red Bull's Max Verstappen to win the race [Reuters] Chief among them is the tension between Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after they contrived to throw away a potential one-two finish in Mexico last Sunday by tangling on the first lap. After that race, Hamilton said the team had "big problems" and needed "serious talks". Those happened on Thursday evening, after Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur arrived back in Brazil having returned to Europe between races. Vasseur said on Friday: "It went well. It was good to discuss. It was good to clarify our positions and now we turn the page. "The guidelines are still the same. They need to respect each other. They are competitive with fighting spirit but they need to respect the other one and the brand and the people working back home and on track. "The message was clear and will stay clear. Overall it is true that they are working for the team and the team has to come first. It's clear we failed and we have to react but the meeting was a clear reminder that Ferrari comes first." item.description: The Sao Paulo Grand Prix weekend last season was attended by 304,000 fans [Getty Images] The 2026 Formula 1 season heads from Mexico City straight to Interlagos in Brazil for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, from 6-8 November. Italian Kimi Antonelli is the new drivers' world champion after sealing the title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver is now the youngest world champion in the history of F1, beating previous record holder Sebastian Vettel by three years. Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in Mexico, with Lewis Hamilton finishing second. The victory lifts Dutchman Verstappen to second in the standings, two points ahead of Ferrari's Hamilton. In Sao Paulo on Friday, McLaren's Lando Norris was the fastest driver in first practice and Antonelli topped the times in the second session. Esteban Ocon won't be in Brazil after being dropped by Haas for the rest of the season. Brazilian 21-year-old Rafael Camara, who is set to join the team in 2027, comes in for the race in Sao Paulo. item.title: Oilers first NHL team to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie
item.description: EDMONTON, CANADA - NOVEMBER 5: Emergency backup goaltender (EBUG) Brett Epp #00 of the Edmonton Oilers stands for the singing of the national anthem prior to the game against the Anaheim Ducks at Rogers Place on November 5, 2026, in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. (Photo by Andy Devlin/NHLI via Getty Images) NHLI via Getty Images EDMONTON, Alberta (AP) — The Edmonton Oilers became the first NHL team to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie Thursday night for their game against against Anaheim. Brett Epp was in uniform while fourth-string goalie Matt Tomkins started for the Oilers. Tristan Jarry was out due to illness and Devon Levi and Frederik Andersen are injured. This is the first season NHL teams have been required to have EBUGs on rosters. The goaltenders, who travel with their club and wear No. 00, can’t have previously played in the NHL under a standard contract, must have 80 games or less of professional experience, and can’t have suited up professionally over the three preceding campaigns. Before this season, home teams were tasked with providing an EBUG in the event either side suffered an in-game goaltending injury or illness.

item.title: Bundesliga Player Ratings | Hamburg 3-1 Borussia Mönchengladbach
item.description: Bundesliga Player Ratings | Hamburg 3-1 Borussia Mönchengladbach Merlin Polzin’s Hamburg have snapped their three-match losing streak and returned to winning ways with a 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach in the 2026/27 Bundesliga’s matchday nine “curtain-raiser”. A pulsating match at Hamburger SV’s Volksparkstadion fully lived up to its billing with plenty of action and storylines. In the end, however, it is once again Gladbach who must contend with last place in the Bundesliga table after incurring their seventh defeat of the season and third loss in five fixtures under new head coach Alexander Blessin. Both teams welcome back injured central defenders HSV trainer Polzin was once again able to call upon the services of his de facto defensive captain. Center back Sebastiaan Bornauw was one of three changes to the XI that lined up against Eintracht Frankfurt . Bornauw replaced Jordan Torunarigha in a straight swap in the back-three. Zakaria El Ouahdi replaced Louis Lemke, with David Møller Wolfe shifting over to Lemke’s left wingback role. In attack, Patson Daka took over for Terem Moffi to spearhead the attack. On the Gladbach side, the long-injured Ko Itakura returned to the Gladbach XI for his first start since matchday four. Itakura served as Blessin’s lone change from last weekend’s goalless draw against Paderborn. Gladbach start strong, but Muheim strikes again! The guests certainly started the match stronger, creating three opportunities inside the opening ten minutes. Shuto Machino shot wide in the 4th while Fabio Chiarodia saw an effort blocked in the 7th. BMG keeper Daniel Batz found himself in the awkward position of having to bail out teammate Joe Scally in the 8th minute when the resurgent American committed a serious error. Scally’s blind backward header was quickly latched onto by Daka. Somehow, Batz recovered in time to ensure that Scally’s mistake didn’t prove fatal. The action quickly swung back the other way via a Gladbach counterattack. Lukas Ullrich’s finish of a Robin Hack set-up didn’t miss wide left by much. Before 12 minutes had elapsed, however, Hamburg managed to score against the run of play. Swiss international Miro Muheim, in a scene that left all observers rubbing their eyes in disbelief, managed to top his other two sparkling distance goals of the current season with a positively absurd diamond-cutter from 30 meters out. Muheim’s powerful strike moved like a guided missile into the top right corner. The Hanseatic hosts went up 1-0 on a serious “Goal of the Season” candidate! Two teams exchange blows under the lights Muheim’s goal pumped the match full of energy, and the action absolutely would not abate. Muheim, understandably, rode his fiery form and produced two more efforts before the opening half was through. Scally, meanwhile, sought redemption in the form of two shots, two assisted shots, and plenty of direct sprints into the box. Batz did well to directly parry efforts in front of his net (14th, 43rd)

item.title: Serie A | Venezia 2-1 Udinese: Kike Pérez stunner spoils Zanetti’s debut
item.description: Serie A | Venezia 2-1 Udinese: Kike Pérez stunner spoils Zanetti’s debut Kike Pérez hit a superb long-range winner as Venezia beat Udinese 2-1 at the Penzo, spoiling Paolo Zanetti’s first game as Udinese coach against his former club and sending the Friuliani to the bottom of Serie A . Zanetti was appointed earlier this week after Kosta Runjaic was sacked. Udinese had taken one point from their previous eight league games and went into this relegation six-pointer one point above Davide Nicola’s Venezia, whose only win of the season had come against Napoli last month. Venezia started on the front foot, and Antoine Hainaut forced an early save from Maduka Okoye inside the area. Nicolò Zaniolo then wasted a good chance when he found space in the box and shot wide. The hosts kept pushing. Juan Jesus headed a corner just over and Pasquale Mazzocchi curled a long-range effort inches wide. At the other end, Filip Stanković kept out Jurgen Ekkelenkamp. Hainaut had the best chance of the half when he collected a rebound and fired over, and it stayed 0-0 at the break. VENICE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 06: Kike Perez celebrates with his teammates after scoring his team’s advantage goal during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and Udinese Calcio at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on November 06, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Udinese pay the price as Venezia snatch three points Udinese should have led early in the second half. Keinan Davis went one-on-one with Stanković inside the six-yard box, but the Venezia goalkeeper made a fine save to deny him. It proved costly, as Venezia went ahead in the 54th minute. Hainaut crossed from the right and Toma Bašić finished low into the bottom corner. The lead lasted only three minutes. Matías Moreno diverted the ball into his own net, and the equaliser stood after a long VAR check on Zaniolo’s position in the build-up. Pérez restored the hosts’ lead in the 65th minute, picking up Mazzocchi’s pass and sending a left-footed shot from outside the box into the top corner, leaving Okoye with no chance. Mazzocchi was forced off injured soon afterwards, and Udinese looked for a way back. Stanković saved well from substitute Giorgi Chakvetadze’s long-range shot. Venezia nearly made the game safe from a corner, when Moreno headed wide and Simon Sohm had a shot blocked, and Akor Adams had a goal ruled out for offside with nine minutes left. The win lifts Venezia off the bottom, a point behind Monza. Zanetti’s Udinese drop to last place, and both sides return after the international break: Venezia visit Juventus on 22 November at 12:30 CET [11:30 GMT], while Udinese travel to Bologna at 15:00 CET [14:00 GMT]. item.title: One of state's top basketball players returns from prep school for senior season
item.description: Devin Bolden, an Indiana Junior All-Star and City Player of the Year last season at Cardinal Ritter, reenrolled at Ritter this week after leaving for an East Coast prep school following his junior year. The 6-foot-8 Bolden, who averaged 20.9 points, 12.6 rebounds and 1.4 blocked shots as a junior for Ritter, had planned to play his senior year at Rocktop Academy in the Philadelphia area. Former Ritter coach Derrick Williams was at Rocktop Academy but is no longer after his mother passed away last month. Ritter athletic director Levar Johnson confirmed that Bolden has enrolled at Ritter, which finished 14-13 last season and won a sectional championship. Former assistant Steven Lopez is now the Raiders’ coach. “He’s back (at Ritter) and our focus is on moving forward,” Bolden’s father C.J. Bolden said Friday. “Things didn’t work out like we hoped staying at Rocktop like we planned initially. But we’re focused on moving forward and doing what’s best for Devin moving forward.” Johnson said he expects Bolden to be cleared for full athletic eligibility by the Indiana High School Athletic Association. Under the IHSAA rules, a student whose “second transfer involves a return to the IHSAA Member School where they established their initial promotion eligibility will retain full eligibility within 365 days of their enrollment date at the previous school.” Bolden scored 1,278 career points in his first three seasons at Ritter. The Raiders won a sectional championship last season for the first time in 17 years. Call Star reporter Kyle Neddenriep at (317) 444-6649. item.title: Blue Jays Denounce Anthony Santander’s Islamophobic Videos About Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Anthony Santander Credit: Jane Gershovich/MLB Photos via Getty NEED TO KNOW Toronto Blue Jays issued a statement after outfielder Anthony Santander reposted Islamophobic videos The two videos, shared on Santander’s Instagram Stories, included an image of Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed In 2023, the team cut ties with another player, Anthony Bass, after he shared anti-LGBTQ sentiments on social media Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander is under fire for incendiary comments he made on social media following the election of Abdul El-Sayed. On his Instagram Stories on Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Venezuelan All-Star shared two Islamophobic videos , one which claimed, “America voted for Sharia last night,” featuring an image of El-Sayed, and another that said, “Islam is not peaceful.” The posts were later deleted. On Tuesday, El-Sayed, 42, defeated Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. In the wake of Santander’s posts, the Blue Jays released a statement shared with PEOPLE. Anthony Santander Credit: Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty “Baseball is for everyone,” the statement read, “and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization’s values and beliefs.” El-Sayed repeatedly dealt with anti-Islamic rhetoric during his campaign, which he ended up handedly winning by 7%. He reflected on the Islamophobic attacks during an appearance on The View on Thursday. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “They weren’t attacking me. They were attacking the idea of an America big enough for me,” El-Sayed told the co-hosts. “I didn’t take a bet on my abilities or anything. The Flyers defeated the Wild 3-2 in the shootout. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty Images ST. PAUL, Minn. (AP) — Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber returned to practice with the team on Thursday, moving closer to making his regular season debut that was delayed by a fractured skull. Wild coach John Hynes said Faber has been cleared by team doctors to play, but the 24-year-old still needs to ramp up his strength and conditioning to be ready for game action. Faber won’t play in either of Minnesota’s home games on Friday or Saturday, Hynes said, but he’s scheduled to be on the next road trip that begins on Tuesday at Montreal. Faber was hit on the side of his helmet near the left ear hole by a shot in a preseason game on Sept. 25 and later taken to a hospital for surgery after his condition worsened. Faber logged the ninth-most minutes of any player in the NHL last season and had a career-high 51 points in 80 games. The Wild lead the Central Division with 25 points at 11-3-3, despite the absence of Faber and other key players to injuries. Captain Jared Spurgeon, who replaced Faber on the top defensive pair with Quinn Hughes, suffered a lower-body injury and has missed the last seven games. Spurgeon will also join the Wild for the road trip next week along with forwards Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno and goalie Filip Gustavsson, who has yet to play this season while recovering from hip surgery. The Foligno brothers have each been out for a month due to upper body injuries.

item.title: Von Miller reveals why Colts are 'scary' matchup for Cowboys in Week 9
item.description: Von Miller reveals why Colts are 'scary' matchup for Cowboys in Week 9 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys are currently 3-5 following a brutal loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8. They blew the lead and lost in overtime. Brian Schottenheimer stayed on as the head coach, and the Cowboys now desperately need a win to get back on track. Fortunately, the Cowboys face one of the worst teams in the NFL, the Indianapolis Colts . The Colts are 2-6 on the season, and they've begun to ship off key pieces. This game should be an easy one for the Cowboys. However, Von Miller doesn't see it that way. Todd Archer of ESPN shared that Miller believes the Colts are a "scary" opponent for the Cowboys, as the players on that Colts team are "fighting for their lives" right now. Von Miller reveals why Colts are a 'scary' matchup for Cowboys "Those guys are fighting for their lives as well," Miller said. "They're trying to find their identity, too. And those teams are always scary whenever you play them because you really don't know what to expect." At first glance, Miller calling the Colts a "scary" team makes no sense. The Jacksonville Jaguars just blew them out 42-7 in Week 8. Why should any team be scared of them, especially with Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner traded away? But, as Miller noted, this Colts team could come out firing on all cylinders for what might be the last time of this era before the trade deadline shakes things up. Would it really be a huge surprise if Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Daniel Jones, and Tyler Warren put together a big day against the Cowboys in what is likely to be their last game together? MORE : Jerry Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer after Cowboys collapse vs. Cardinals No, it wouldn't be a surprise even after their horrible Week 8 performance. The Dallas defense has struggled this season, and these Colts players are trying to either keep their jobs or prove themselves worthy of being traded for by a top contender. The flip side of this is that there's a non-zero chance that the Colts, seeing the fire sale on the horizon, struggle to muster much of anything all game and have a disappointing performance in the last game of this era of Colts football. Such high variance is what has Miller scared. There's a chance this Colts team plays horribly, and it's an easy Cowboys win. But there is a very real chance that the Cowboys face a motivated Colts team making one last stand together before they're separated. So, while Miller pointing out the Colts as a "scary" team might sound ridiculous at first, there is good reason to be worried. This is a classic "trap game" for the Cowboys, or any team that faces the Colts or a looming seller at the trade deadline. item.title: SNY cancels shows, guts website amid significant layoffs
item.description: Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect SportsNet New York, the TV home of the New York Mets often referred to as SNY, carried out layoffs that will gut its website and cancel a significant amount of original network programming. Andrew Marchand and Marc Carig of The Athletic were first to report the news Friday afternoon. According to The Athletic, SNY has canceled Baseball Night in New York and Sportsnite in the wake of Friday’s layoffs, which went into effect immediately. SNY will retain Mets Hot Stove , as well as continue to produce pre and postgame shows for the Mets and New York Jets. According to The Athletic, reporters Chelsea Janes, Ian Begley and Connor Hughes will remain with the network, while much of its talent and editorial staff were let go. The Mets are owned by Steve Cohen, who is one of the richest owners in Major League Baseball, but SNY is still controlled by Sterling Equities, an investment firm owned by the Wilpon and Katz families. The Wilpons, of course, were notoriously cheap during their reign with the Mets. Last year, SNY was reportedly exploring a possible sale , listing Cohen as a potential interested buyer. SNY has a current broadcast agreement with the Mets that extends through 2035, making Cohen seem like a strong candidate. Without finding a buyer, SNY is now undergoing significant layoffs. SNY’s original programming has always been lauded for its honest coverage. Keith Hernandez has even credited Fred Wilpon for encouraging network talent to be honest about the Mets.
